minutes.headline: School calendar for next year approved over objections to the two-week December break; trips and contracts also approved.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the superintendent's report, gave final approval to the New York music trip and the Latin convention, and initial approval to an Italy and Greece trip. It declared surplus property, approved the draft calendar after a motion to table failed, authorized signing the special ed transport contract and the collaborative agreement, accepted donations, appointed a member to the building reuse committee, and went to executive session on bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Public comment opened; a speaker announced a Boys and Girls Club fundraiser event and remembered a late school council member (taken up again at 4645).

what_happened.line: The committee approved the draft 2014-15 school calendar after a motion to table it for more information failed.
A motion to table the calendar failed; a fall discussion on the calendar and break structure is to be scheduled.
Final approval passed for the New York City music trip, and initial approval passed for the Italy and Greece trip.
The budget hearing is to be held next week, once more is known on special education placements and retirements.
Special education tuitions are running above the initial budget and are being managed with other savings.

why_it_matters: The calendar sets the 2014-15 school year for families, including the length of the December break, and the committee plans a fall discussion on the break structure.

Special education tuitions above budget, with state circuit breaker reimbursement arriving after the placement cost, put pressure on the school budget that feeds the town budget, which is mostly taxes.
watch_next: The school budget hearing, planned for the week after this meeting, once special education placements and retirements are clearer.
The fall discussion on the school calendar and break structure, and the next meeting where members bring calendars to schedule workshops.
